quest.title: The Empty Illusions of the Sabzeruz Festival
quest.description: In your memory, you never seem to have tried to go outside the city, which is curious.\nToday you decide to try...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x625, Primogem x30, Mora x25450, Hero's Wit x2, Mystic Enhancement Ore x4

chapter.title: The Morn a Thousand Roses Brings

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...Our memories are back!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Let's go and try to leave the city today.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...About that... Well, where should Paimon begin...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Huh? Paimon, what do you mean?

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Traveler, aside from your memories that were just restored, I have another message for you.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Another message? From who?

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Listen to it and you'll understand.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: "...Can't go back... There are countless spaces here. Our Sabzeruz Festival in Sumeru City is just one of them..."

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: This is... my own voice!?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Traveler, you should be missing two days' worth of memories. Paimon will fill you in...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Two days ago.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...It's time to carry out our plan from yesterday!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Let's go and try to leave the city today.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Okay, let's go!

talks.objective: Head to the city gate to find a way out

dialogues.speaker: Merchant
dialogues.text: ...Why can't we leave the city? What is the Akademiya up to now?

dialogues.speaker: Guard
dialogues.text: Don't ask me. It's not like I can tell you anything. This is a direct order from the Grand Sage. Just wait until tomorrow.

dialogues.speaker: Merchant
dialogues.text: I have a real emergency. My goods have already arrived at Port Ormos. If I don't hurry, they'll be stolen...

dialogues.speaker: Guard
dialogues.text: That's your problem. Make sure you make a request in advance next time.

dialogues.speaker: Merchant
dialogues.text: B—But it's not like you can just predict business matters in advance... *sigh*

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It looks like the Akademiya already announced a lockdown for Sumeru City today. How completely unsurprising...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Let's go and question them.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hello sir, why can't we leave the city today?

dialogues.speaker: Guard
dialogues.text: Here we go again... Don't ask me, I don't know either.

dialogues.speaker: Guard
dialogues.text: We just received an order that no one is allowed to enter or exit Sumeru today. They didn't tell us anything else.

choices.text: Of course the Akademiya wouldn't share their plans with a pawn.

response.speaker: Guard
response.text: Hmph, angering me won't get you anywhere. If I had that kind of insider info, I would have left this stupid post a long time ago.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It looks like he really doesn't know.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: If we can't get anything out of him, let's take matters into our own hands. Why don't we climb over the walls? Those guards can't be everywhere at once.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: This is a good spot, and the guard hasn't noticed us at all. Let's hurry...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Paimon, stay here.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh!? Why? Are you going to leave Paimon behind?

choices.text: Leaving the city might trigger disruptions to our memories...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: B—But what if things get really weird out there and you get into some trouble? Th—Then Paimon won't be able to help you!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ugh... Paimon knows that Paimon can't do much, but we've always been together, haven't we?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...Okay, Paimon will wait for you.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Promise Paimon that you'll come back as soon as possible. Just a quick look!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Okay, okay...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: And please be careful!

choices.text: If we leave together, it'll just be the same as before.
We need someone to stay and witness events from this side.
So the Akademiya doesn't trust you at all.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ah... Memories...!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Let's go and try to leave the city today.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Traveler! W—W—Waaaaaah!!!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Wh—What's wrong, Paimon!?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon thought Paimon would never see you again! Y—You just disappeared!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon waited for you for hours and hours at the city wall, and you never came back! You promised Paimon that you were only taking a quick look! *sniff*

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Wh—What did I promise?

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: #Paimon, calm down. {F#She's}{M#He's} here now. I don't think {F#she}{M#he} understood what you were saying.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: *sniff*... Paimon doesn't care. Paimon wanted to go look for you, but you also said that Paimon should stay... Paimon was so worried and so scared the entire day...

choices.text: Although I don't remember doing any of this...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I won't leave you behind.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: *sniff* ...Okay, Paimon will forgive you. The most important thing is that you didn't actually disappear... Paimon was so scared that you had gone into another world!

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Okay, Paimon, can you tell us your perspective of what really happened yesterday...

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Paimon describes your plan from yesterday...

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: I see. Using two people's different perspectives...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: After that, you left the city. Paimon kept her eyes on you the whole time, but then you disappeared in an instant...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: You sure that's what you saw? You weren't zoning out or anything?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: No way! Paimon was watching you with the fullest attention.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: What's your perspective, Traveler? You sure you don't have any memory of this?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Yes, I don't even know that "yesterday" existed.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: I guess that explains everything. You also lost your memories the last two times you tried to leave the city. Those days' memories can't be awoken.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So if we leave the city, our memories will be completely erased?

choices.text: So they didn't just restrict access to Sumeru City...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It really sounds like something big outside of the city is being hidden on purpose!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But this way, we'll also never discover what's outside...

choices.text: If our memories will be erased...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Something like a message? But how can we send it back?

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: ...Don't look at me like that. I... I'm not used to being stared at.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Well... Okay, okay. You want something that can pass on messages, right? Give me some time, and take care of Dunyarzad for me.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yep! Now we're talking!

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: ...I'm done. Here you go.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What? Isn't this just an Akasha Terminal?

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: I made some little changes. Akasha Terminals are already capable of sending messages. I just tweaked it so that it can connect to any node.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: To make something like this... Nahida, you really know the Akasha like the back of your hand! Anyway, we can use this now to record a message, right?

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Yep. I will help you save the messages. It should be pretty easy to use. I just can't guarantee the user's status and signal coverage when they're outside the city...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We'll never know until we try! At least we're taking the initiative now!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: It's worth a try.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Let's go then. Let's expose those sages!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I still think you should stay.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ahh... Alright. Paimon isn't as worried about being separated since it happened once yesterday, but... Paimon still isn't happy about it...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: See you tomorrow, Paimon.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Okay! See you tomorrow, Traveler!

choices.text: Can we leave behind something other than memories?
They're also erasing the memories of those who leave...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ohh, so that's what it is! After the sound of the beep, the final space — the Sabzeruz Festival — also disappears, and we're taken to the next day.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Later on, Traveler also mentioned a bunch of new spaces materializing behind them... Do lots of new spaces appear every day?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon's head is spinning... Just what are these "spaces," anyhow?

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Well, consider this, for all the horrors of the Archon War, at its heart, it was just a game where a bunch of gods fought over seven seats.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: So no matter how strange or spooky things might look on the surface, maybe all they point to in the end is a small and simple secret.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow, the Archon War, huh? That's an analogy and a half.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: A "secret," huh...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Give me some time. I need to organize my thoughts.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, where are you going?

talks.objective: Organize your thoughts on the familiar bench in the city

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Do you want some alone time to think? Alright then, Paimon won't disturb you.

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: ...The Dance of Sabzeruz is about to begin. I'm going to go watch it.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: The Dance of Sabzeruz... It's that time already...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Okay, um... Why don't you go ahead, Dunyarzad? We still have some other stuff to do first.

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: Okay then. See you later.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Have you figured it out yet, Traveler? Time is ticking away.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I think I know the answer now.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Awesome! What is it? Paimon wants to know! ...Wait, no, let's meet up with Nahida first. You can tell us both together. This time, we're gonna get to the truth!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I don't have any more questions.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Deceiving the people of Sumeru with no regard for their safety... No matter what they're trying to do, this is unforgivable.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: After we end the Sabzeruz Festival samsara, we have to look into them...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: How can the sages of the Akademiya do this behind their Archon's back? This is ridiculous!

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: In the end, I'm just the Moon. The real Sun is long gone.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: A Sun and a Moon... Nahida's talking in riddles again...
*beep*

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, we're out of time today.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: I'll tell you how to break free of the samsara tomorrow. See you then...

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Correct. The Akasha is keeping each person's brain in a constant dream state, but also separating their consciousness from their own dream.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Their disembodied consciousness is placed inside the collective dream of the Sabzeruz Festival along with everyone else's, while their now-vacant dreams are harvested by the Akasha.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: No one is any the wiser as another day passes in the dream, and so begins another samsara cycle...

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: People "wake up" to yet another dream about the Sabzeruz Festival, the dreams that belong to them are once again harvested by the Akasha... and so it continues.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So... this is like a dream factory, and the Akasha is... a dream-harvesting machine. Did Paimon get that analogy right?

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Very good, Paimon. Using analogies well is an excellent habit to get into.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Okay, so that beep we keep hearing is actually from our real-life Akasha Terminals... Taking off our terminals in this dream doesn't do anything...

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Alright, last question... Who am I?

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Hehe. So you noticed.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You are Lesser Lord Kusanali.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Aww, I thought that one would be the hardest question. That's why I put it last.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Pff, that wasn't hard at all. Even Paimon guessed that! Everything about you is different. We just didn't wanna expose you is all.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Now that you mention it... Nahida, you've been hinting to us since the very beginning...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It's funny thinking back to when we were asking all over the place for info about Lesser Lord Kusanali. Paimon didn't expect to meet you like this!

choices.text: I have a lot of questions for you.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Yes, those can wait until we're back in real life.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: On the other hand, I'd be happy to answer any more questions you have about here and now.

choices.text: But this doesn't seem like a good time.

dialogues.speaker: Guard
dialogues.text: Hey! Stop right there! No one is allowed to enter or leave Sumeru City right now. Go away!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa... Ugh, okay.

dialogues.speaker: Guard
dialogues.text: Hey! Stop right there! No one is allowed to enter or leave Sumeru City right now. Go away!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa... Ugh, okay.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: We don't have many more festivals to waste. Hurry and find the truth.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...That covers everything that's happened so far.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Yes. Although the signal was choppy and had some interference, we still managed to receive two messages from you when you were outside.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Okay, now that you understand what's going on, let's hear the messages together!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: "...Can't go back... There are countless spaces here. Our Sabzeruz Festival in Sumeru City is just one of them..."

response.speaker: Player
response.text: "...I've entered another space... Before me are flowing sandstone and howling fish... Impossible and surreal sights..."

response.speaker: Player
response.text: "...All these spaces are empty except for the occasional ones that contain mute puppets rather than people... I can't sense any human presence..."

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...That's one heck of an info dump! It sounds like you left the Sumeru City space when you set foot outside of the walls.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...But everything looked completely normal when Paimon was looking out from the inside! That's unbelievable. And if we take your word for it, the other spaces all had very weird contents...

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: There's one final part here... I only received it late last night.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: ...These spaces have been disappearing one after the other... Absorbed by something like a sun in the sky...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: *beep* ...And now, even the final space has also disappeared...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: ...Behind me, a lot of spaces just appeared again from thin air... I get it now! Those spaces are actually—

response.speaker: Player
response.text: *buzz*

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ah... Ugh, why did the message end right there? What did the Traveler want to say? What are those spaces?

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Probably because "yesterday" just happened to end at that moment.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, right, Paimon did hear a beep from the Akasha. Did it come from here or from the message?

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: The message. It should've come from the Traveler's Akasha Terminal.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: After the beep, Traveler said, "Even the final space has also disappeared..."

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Traveler, what do you think that "final space" could have been?

choices.text: Was what I left for myself when I left the city?

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: You're back. I've been waiting forever for you two. Judging by the looks on your faces...

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Are you ready to take your Sabzeruz Exam and graduate from the festival?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Ask away, Miss Nahida.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Hehe, okay, first off... Have you discovered the hidden truth?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: People in Sumeru think they don't dream, but the truth is, the Akasha steals their dreams without them knowing it.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #And those spaces with no human presence are stolen dreams without their host? That would explain why they sounded so weird when {F#she}{M#he} was trying to describe them...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh, so people in Sumeru do dream after all. In fact, we're all in one big dream together right now!

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Correct answer. Now, how did you conclude that the Akasha is capable of this?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ooh, okay. Those dream-controlling creatures in the forest also get their power from the Dendro Archon, right? That would explain why the Akasha has the ability to control people's dreams, too.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But... is stealing everyone's dreams really how the Akasha compiles their wisdom? Isn't there anything more to it than that?

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Dreams are fantastical, complex, and full of imagination. People's brains are the most active when they're dreaming.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: In other words, dreams are rich bundles of human wisdom.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So in other words, the complete opposite of how Haypasia understood it...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon remembers her saying that the sages think dreams are "foolish delusions," and the fact that no one dreams is a blessing from Greater Lord Rukkhadevata... Hmph, so it was all a dirty trick!?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The real story is that the sages from the Akademiya are using the Akasha to steal people's dreams for their own use, huh?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Yes, and they don't intend to stop there.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Oh? By the sounds of it, you understand the current situation pretty well. So then, what about this samsara?

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: "Celebrate the birth of that god"...

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Could it mean...

dialogues.speaker: Merchant
dialogues.text: *sigh* Can you understand the feeling of having Mora slip right through your fingers? How can these people be so unreasonable...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Why couldn't you simply tell us the truth?

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: You asked me this question before. My answer was: "It would literally blow your minds."

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Now that you know this is all a dream, this answer should hopefully make more sense...

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Have you heard the saying "Don't wake a sleepwalker"? Likewise, if someone suddenly had told you all of this instead of you learning it on your own...

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Your notion of reality and dream would be thrown into irreversible confusion. I couldn't expose you to that kind of risk.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: That's why I could only give you very subtle hints and some suggestions. Long story short, I'm really sorry I had to keep you guessing.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: How do the sages manage to keep people from noticing this?

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Firstly, this dream we're in is completely based on reality. People have already experienced this Sabzeruz Festival, so it would be very difficult for them to find anything that strikes them as surreal.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Secondly, you're probably wondering why people don't have any memories from earlier samsara, right?

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: That's because people don't remember their dreams most of the time anyway. And in any case, their actual dreams are being taken away from them by the Akasha...

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: So whenever they "wake up" in this dream of the Sabzeruz Festival, they don't remember anything from their previous, identical dream.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That reminds Paimon. Traveler had a dream when we were in the Avidya Forest, but couldn't say what it was about after waking up. Is that an example of what you mean?

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Yes. Only after receiving the blessing of Dendro can a person gain the Dendro element's dream-enhancing power. That explains the feelings of déjà vu.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Meanwhile, everyone else has no idea that they are in a Sabzeruz Festival samsara while their dreams are stolen from them over and over again.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About the side effects of a "mass-produced dream"...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Can humans really keep dreaming forever like this? Will it ever end? And if so, when?

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: You might say your mental fatigue has already answered this question. Eventually, there is only so much that people can tolerate.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Especially those whose health is compromised to begin with... like Dunyarzad. This relentless exploitation takes an even harder toll on them.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: People's lives are at stake here, and nobody knows a thing... We've gotta put a stop to this!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Why is the dream about the Sabzeruz Festival?

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: I know, right? Why did they have to base this dream on my birthday? Could it really just be a coincidence?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Even you don't know the reason? Wow, now that's strange.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: The Akademiya's sages are determined to harvest lots of dreams in a short time, no matter the cost. They have to be up to no good. Unfortunately, I don't know anything about it.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Traveler, do you have any information?

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Well, consider this, for all the horrors of the Archon War, at its heart, it was just a game where a bunch of gods fought over seven seats.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: So no matter how strange or spooky things might look on the surface, maybe all they point to in the end is a small and simple secret.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: The Moon, illusions, and lies... What do they all mean?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What's happening right now seems to have happened before. This feeling has been getting stronger and stronger...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: The Grand Sage said, "Go celebrate the birth of that god to your heart's content." Did he mean something more?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Dehya sold her greatsword to raise additional funds, and she was injured because she wasn't used to her new weapon.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: My mind feels exhausted, even though I haven't done too much thinking. What is going on?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We've already experienced the Sabzeruz Festival many times. And... the day of the festival seems to be in a perpetual samsara.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: People in Sumeru don't dream. What a strange phenomenon.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Okay, Nahida said, "The Akasha relies on the power of a Gnosis to operate, as it is the manifestation of the God of Wisdom's power. It compiles the wisdom of the entire populace, and it grants knowledge to the people."

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Mercenaries rely heavily on muscle memory, and Dehya was able to use her experiences to avoid injury in later samsara cycles.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: The beep is a prompt tone for Akasha operations. We still hear it every night, even though we removed our Akasha Terminals.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: All the bizarre spaces I saw outside the city had one thing in common: a lack of human presence.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Those spaces remind me of... dreams. Like the one I had in the Avidya Forest, except these have no sign of human presence.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Those spaces kept disappearing before my eyes, but as soon as that beep sounded, many more spaces materialized.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Those dreamscapes kept vanishing, but as soon as that beep sounded, more new spaces appeared.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: ..Was that space actually the real world? But wouldn't a real space just randomly disappearing like that be catastrophic?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: My impression is that each day in this samsara only ends at the sound of that beep from the Akasha.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: That should be it... The flow of time is endlessly cycling within one single day.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: If all our memories of a day are erased at the end of that day, then we would unwittingly relive the same day again and again.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We are all in a dream. It isn't that the people of Sumeru don't dream. Rather, the Akasha is taking their dreams from them.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: The Akasha relies on the power of a Gnosis to operate.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: It is a manifestation of the God of Wisdom's power.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
